newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Thousands await Zaire rebel leader in Mbuji-Mayi.
newsitem.headline: Thousands await Zaire rebel leader in Mbuji-Mayi.

text.p: Thousands of people gathered in Zaire's diamond capital on Monday to welcome rebel chief Laurent Kabila and a mining official said looters left untouched diamond stores at the country's only modern mine.

"There was pillage at the mine. We haven't done an inventory so don't know how much but they didn't break into the diamond storehouses," Mfwamba Tchobobo, director of Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA), told Reuters.
MIBA is Zaire's only modern mine and officially produces diamonds worth about $80 million annually. MIBA dominates the economy at Mbuji-Mayi and is Zaire's biggest foreign exchange earner.

Residents said government troops fled the city on Friday after looting and the first rebels of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) had arrived later the same day and were reinforced on Saturday.
There were no signs of any damage at Mbuji-Mayi airport where about 2,000 people gathered to meet Kabila. Few rebels were visible except for the rebel chief's bodyguards.

"There was no fighting in the city. On Saturday, people came and welcomed the liberators and carried their weapons," said Tshikala Ndaie, a priest and vicar-general of the Liberal Catholic Church of Congo.
